Yes — this is the friendlier everyday version I had in mind. Tapping "design" to include it, then tapping "accessibility" until it flips to "Not accessibility," gave me the same three links as the typed command, but I never had to remember any punctuation or special words. I could just see my choices lit up — this one in, that one out — and read back what I'd asked for. If I fumble, I just tap again to change it. That's the kind of thing I'd actually use without thinking.

Comparing the two: they land on the same result, which is what matters, but this point-and-click one is what I'd reach for day to day. I'd still keep the typed way for when someone wants to move fast — it's not wrong, just not my instinct. So, like the label filtering, ideally both live side by side: click-to-build for me, typed for speed.

This is the everyday approach I wanted.
